goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb remove_member passes an Integer to group.users.delete instead of a record object, so the membership is not removed

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` and then calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. `group.users` is an ActiveRecord association collection, and `delete` on a collection is intended to be passed record objects (e.g., a `User`), not a raw Integer id. Passing an Integer will not reliably remove the membership and in common Rails versions will raise `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` (since it checks the class of each "record" argument), so the membership removal can fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs uses {{#unless automatic}} in the member context where automatic doesn't resolve, so the remove link renders for automatic groups
admin/groups_controller.rb update/create coerce a missing visible param to false, silently flipping group visibility on partial updates

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update the code unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. If the request omits the `visible` parameter (a partial update), `params[:visible]` is nil, the expression evaluates to false, and a previously-visible group will be silently flipped to invisible on save. This is directly verifiable in the diff because alias_level is guarded with `if params[:alias_level].present?` while visible is not. (Create similarly defaults to false when visible is missing.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members takes limit from user params with no upper bound, allowing the entire membership to be serialized

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no maximum cap. This means a caller can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g., very large integer) and cause the server to query/serialize a huge number of members in one response, potentially returning the entire membership list and creating a performance/DoS risk. The lack of an upper bound is verifiable from the new code.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the function can return undefined on some code paths (e.g., an early return when input is empty / missing explicit return), which can break callers expecting a value/promise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members passes a negative offset through unvalidated to .offset(), producing a SQL error

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the code sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then unconditionally calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. If a client supplies a negative offset (e.g., `?offset=-10`), `to_i` yields `-10` and ActiveRecord will generate SQL with a negative OFFSET (e.g., `OFFSET -10`), which is invalid in PostgreSQL and can raise a SQL error. There is no validation/clamping to `>= 0` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(",") assuming a String, so array-form params raise NoMethodError and return 500 instead of 400

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the request supplies `usernames` as an Array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` or JSON array), `params.require(:usernames)` will return an Array, which does not respond to `split`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500. There is no type check/coercion in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin groups_controller specs hardcode id: 1 / group_id: 1 assuming a seeded automatic group, raising RecordNotFound on a differently seeded DB

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce specs that call `xhr :put, :update, id: 1` and `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1` without fabricating a group in the test itself. However, whether this is a real defect (i.e., will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`) depends on an external invariant: that an automatic group with id=1 exists in the test DB (many apps/frameworks seed such groups with fixed IDs). The diff alone does not demonstrate that id=1 will be missing or that IDs are non-deterministic here, so the finding is not verifiably a real problem from this change set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec covers the new paginated members + meta response shape (limit/offset/total), despite it being a breaking payload change

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (an array payload) to a new JSON object shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and the JS model `Group#findMembers` now depends on `result.meta` and `result.members`. In the diff, specs are only modified for `Admin::GroupsController`; there is no spec added/updated to assert the new paginated `members` endpoint response shape or its `meta` fields, so this breaking payload change is not covered by tests in this change set.
